cases.sentence: О, эти ___, лавки, калачи, фонари, извозчики!» думал Ростов, когда уже они записали свои отпуски на заставе и въехали в Москву.
cases.explain: «несносные улицы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “How much longer? How much longer? Oh, these insufferable streets, shops, bakers’ signboards, street lamps, and sleighs!” thought Rostóv, when their leave permits had been passed at the town gate and they had entered Moscow.

cases.sentence: Прокофий, ___, тот, который был так силен, что за задок поднимал карету, сидел и вязал из покромок лапти.
cases.explain: «выездной лакей» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Old Mikháilo was asleep on the chest. Prokófy, the footman, who was so strong that he could lift the back of the carriage from behind, sat plaiting slippers out of cloth selvedges. He looked up at the opening door and his expression of sleepy indifference suddenly changed to one of delighted amazement.

cases.sentence: Соня, Наташа, Петя, Анна Михайловна, Вера, ___, обнимали его; и люди и горничные, наполнив комнаты, приговаривали и ахали.
cases.explain: «старый граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Sónya, Natásha, Pétya, Anna Mikháylovna, Véra, and the old count were all hugging him, and the serfs, men and maids, flocked into the room, exclaiming and oh-ing and ah-ing.

cases.sentence: Соня красная, как кумач, тоже держалась за его руку и вся сияла в ___, устремленном в его глаза, которых она ждала.
cases.explain: «блаженном взгляде» — the prepositional is used only after a preposition, for location or topic.
cases.translation: Sónya too, all rosy red, clung to his arm and, radiant with bliss, looked eagerly toward his eyes, waiting for the look for which she longed. Sónya now was sixteen and she was very pretty, especially at this moment of happy, rapturous excitement. She gazed at him, not taking her eyes off him, and smiling and holding her breath. He gave her a grateful look, but was still expectant and looking for someone. The old countess had not yet come. But now steps were heard at the door, steps so rapid that they could hardly be his mother’s.

cases.sentence: Она не могла поднять лица и только прижимала его к ___ его венгерки.
cases.explain: «холодным снуркам» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Yet it was she, dressed in a new gown which he did not know, made since he had left. All the others let him go, and he ran to her. When they met, she fell on his breast, sobbing. She could not lift her face, but only pressed it to the cold braiding of his hussar’s jacket. Denísov, who had come into the room unnoticed by anyone, stood there and wiped his eyes at the sight.

cases.sentence: Ростов был очень счастлив любовью, которую ему выказывали; но ___ его встречи была так блаженна, что теперешнего его счастия ему казалось мало, и он всё ждал чего-то еще, и еще, и еще.
cases.explain: «первая минута» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Rostóv was very happy in the love they showed him; but the first moment of meeting had been so beatific that his present joy seemed insufficient, and he kept expecting something more, more and yet more.

cases.sentence: В предшествующей комнате валялись сабли, сумки, ташки, раскрытые чемоданы, ___.
cases.explain: «грязные сапоги» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: In the room next to their bedroom there was a confusion of sabers, satchels, sabretaches, open portmanteaus, and dirty boots. Two freshly cleaned pairs with spurs had just been placed by the wall. The servants were bringing in jugs and basins, hot water for shaving, and their well-brushed clothes. There was a masculine odor and a smell of tobacco.

cases.explain: «хриплый голос» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Hallo, Gwíska—my pipe!” came Váska Denísov’s husky voice. “Wostóv, get up!”

cases.sentence: Ростов, протирая слипавшиеся глаза, поднял спутанную голову с ___.
cases.explain: «жаркой подушки» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Rostóv, rubbing his eyes that seemed glued together, raised his disheveled head from the hot pillow.

cases.sentence: — с ___ обратился он к усатому, черному Денисову.
cases.explain: «подобострастным уважением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Is this your saber?” asked Pétya. “Or is it yours?” he said, addressing the black-mustached Denísov with servile deference.

cases.sentence: Ростов почувствовал, как под влиянием ___ любви, в первый раз через полтора года, на душе его и на лице распускалась та детская улыбка, которою он ни разу не улыбался с тех пор, как выехал из дома.
cases.explain: «жарких лучей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Oh, how nice, how splendid!” she said to everything. Rostóv felt that, under the influence of the warm rays of love, that childlike smile which had not once appeared on his face since he left home now for the first time after eighteen months again brightened his soul and his face.

cases.sentence: — Она засучила свой кисейный рукав и показала на своей длинной, худой и нежной ручке под плечом, гораздо выше локтя (в том месте, которое закрыто бывает и ___) красную метину.
cases.explain: «бальными платьями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “No, call her you, please! I’ll tell you all about it some other time. No, I’ll tell you now. You know Sónya’s my dearest friend. Such a friend that I burned my arm for her sake. Look here!” She pulled up her muslin sleeve and showed him a red scar on her long, slender, delicate arm, high above the elbow on that part that is covered even by a ball dress.

cases.sentence: Она была прелестная ___, очевидно страстно его любящая (в этом он не сомневался ни на минуту).
cases.explain: «16-тилетняя девочка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Rostóv saw that it had been well considered by them. Sónya had already struck him by her beauty on the preceding day. Today, when he had caught a glimpse of her, she seemed still more lovely. She was a charming girl of sixteen, evidently passionately in love with him (he did not doubt that for an instant). Why should he not love her now, and even marry her, Rostóv thought, but just now there were so many other pleasures and interests before him! “Yes, they have taken a wise decision,” he thought, “I must remain free.”

cases.sentence: Отчего же ему было не любить ее теперь, и не жениться даже, думал Ростов, но... теперь столько еще ___ и занятий!

cases.explain: «счастливая улыбка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Now?” repeated Natásha, and a happy smile lit up her face. “Have you seen Duport?”

cases.sentence: Денисов, к удивлению Ростова, в ___, напомаженный и надушенный, явился в гостиную таким же щеголем, каким он был в сражениях, и таким любезным с дамами и кавалерами, каким Ростов никак не ожидал его видеть.
cases.explain: «новом мундире» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Véra’s remark was correct, as her remarks always were, but, like most of her observations, it made everyone feel uncomfortable, not only Sónya, Nikoláy, and Natásha, but even the old countess, who—dreading this love affair which might hinder Nikoláy from making a brilliant match—blushed like a girl. Denísov, to Rostóv’s surprise, appeared in the drawing room with pomaded hair, perfumed, and in a new uniform, looking just as smart as he made himself when going into battle, and he was more amiable to the ladies and gentlemen than Rostóv had ever expected to see him.
